correctness.rationale: Direct mean/contrast decomposition is algebraically exact. The range criterion follows from monotonicity of the odd scalar contrast map. Rational derivatives have a unique maximizer for p>1; p<=1 approaches sharp unit slope only at infinity. Gaussian derivative sign reduces to a strictly decreasing scalar root function; substitution gives its sharp constant. The scalar secant/coordinate-swap decomposition extends these constants to every ℓq norm, including endpoint q=1 and infinity. The code independently exercises original two-coordinate formula, slopes, sharp peaks, and 90,000 direct coordinate-norm pair checks. Finite checks are corroborative, not infinite proof.

value.rationale: A natural minimal graph separates classical one-input smoothing from two-input perturbation stability. The result gives a necessary-and-sufficient design rule for all monotone two-point affinities, a sharp critical decay exponent p=1 in the exact rational families previously compared numerically, closed amplification formula independent of bandwidth/coupling scale, and unique Gaussian worst contrast. It also proves one simultaneous stability classification for all ℓq norms. This identifies a reproducible mathematical boundary for nonlinear edge-preserving operators, not an arbitrary tabulation.
